title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows: view two shared screens side by side in meetings
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned room experience and Teams Rooms Pro entitlement. The documented sharing policies and dual monitor controls check out, including the XML setting; the feature's default and room-specific switch remain undocumented.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: No room or tenant switch specifically for displaying two shared screens side by side is documented on the UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Windows multiple screen shares side by side admin setting default rollout 579184; "Teams Rooms" "multiple screen" "settings" XML PowerShell. Read portal settings and searched XML reference; found meeting policy, not a room-layout switch.

claims.claim: No administrator UI setting is documented for AllowMultipleScreenshare.
claims.quote: Searched: AllowMultipleScreenshare Teams admin center meeting options UI policy. Read meeting-policies-content-sharing and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; results document the PowerShell parameter, not an admin UI equivalent.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMultipleScreenshare $false configures availability of Multiple Screenshare meeting options.
claims.quote: **$false**: MultiVBSS meeting options are not available (hidden) for the organizer.

claims.claim: The documented default for AllowMultipleScreenshare is True.
claims.quote:
### -AllowMultipleScreenshare
| Type: | Boolean |
| Default value: | True |

claims.claim: The parameter reference says the feature is not fully released and the setting has no effect.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: The AllowMultipleScreenshare parameter documentation does not state its effect on Teams Rooms receiving or laying out two shares.
claims.quote: Searched: AllowMultipleScreenshare Teams admin center meeting options UI policy; "Teams Rooms" "multiple screen" "settings" XML PowerShell. Read the full AllowMultipleScreenshare parameter section; it describes organiser options, not Teams Rooms behaviour.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Content sharing > Screen sharing mode reaches the documented setting.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**.
2. Select the policy that you want to edit.
3. Go to the **Content sharing** section.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ScreenSharingMode Disabled prohibits screen sharing for the assigned user.
claims.quote: Set this to Disabled to prohibit the user from sharing their screens.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Screen sharing mode is a per-user policy governing desktop and window sharing rather than a room display-layout setting.
claims.quote: This setting is a per-user policy. The setting controls whether a user can share a desktop and window in a Teams meeting.

claims.claim: Teams Rooms Pro Management portal > Rooms > device > Settings > Device > Dual monitor mode reaches the Windows dual monitor setting.
claims.quote: **Teams Rooms on Windows:** In the Pro Management portal, go to **Settings** > **Device** > **Dual monitor mode**.

claims.claim: Setting the DualScreenMode element in SkypeSettings.xml to true enables dual screen mode.
claims.quote: | `<DualScreenMode>` | Boolean ❷ | First ❶ | If true, dual screen mode is enabled. Otherwise the device uses single screen mode. |

claims.where: controls[3].note; Why it matters; Scope: Displays
claims.claim: Dual monitor mode is disabled by default.
claims.quote: | Dual Monitor mode | Toggle | Disabled by default. | Dual screen mode is enabled. Otherwise, the device uses single screen mode. Available for Individual or bulk changes. |

claims.claim: Dual monitor mode is configurable per device.
claims.quote:
Go to **Rooms/ Phones in the left navigation** and click the device you want to configure.
2. Select the **Settings** tab in the device panel.
3. Use the left navigation in the device panels to browse settings categories (About, Account, Meetings, Device, Network, etc.).

claims.claim: Configuring device settings in the Pro Management portal requires its Rooms Management role-based access control permissions.
claims.quote: you can configure settings for Microsoft Teams devices (Teams Rooms on Windows, Teams Rooms on Android, Teams Panels and Teams Phones), provided you have the necessary role-based access control permissions for Rooms Management.

claims.claim: Portal settings management applies only to signed-in devices.
claims.quote: **Settings management is available only for signed-in devices.** Ensure that the device is signed in for settings changes from the Teams Rooms Pro management portal to be applied successfully.

claims.claim: The XML configuration page says Microsoft no longer publishes new XML settings and all settings are manageable in the portal.
claims.quote: We no longer publish new XML settings but all settings are managable within the Portal.

claims.claim: The Pro Management portal's Rooms and Inventory views expose device licensing status through the License Type column.
claims.quote:
Go to **Rooms** and **Inventory** views.
3. In both views, locate the **License Type** column to see device licensing status.

claims.claim: Microsoft's description identifies no new data access beyond displaying the shared meeting screens.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms Windows multiple screen shares side by side admin setting default rollout 579184; "Teams Rooms" "two shared screens". Read roadmap, release notes and room-planning-guidance; no feature-specific new data access is described.
